keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no area (infobox: none); it names an enclave within modern Yogyakarta City and the southern coastal districts of Kulon Progo, 'known as Adikarta Regency until its merger with Kulon Progo in the 1950s'. A 6 km disc and a 25 km disc stand in for them.

ledger.note: 17 March 1813: the Pakualaman is established. Prince Notokusumo was crowned 'by Governor-General Sir Thomas Stamford Raffles' as Kangjeng Gusti Pangeran Adipati, and the principality was established 'on March 17, 1813'; its land was an enclave in Yogyakarta and Adikarta on the Kulon Progo coast, 'a minor Javanese princely state within the Sultanate of Yogyakarta'.

sources.title: Pakualaman
sources.note: Founding 17 March 1813 under Raffles, the enclave and Adikarta, status 1813-1816 (British), 1816-1942 (Dutch dependent state), 1942-1945 (Japanese), 1945 Republic.

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch at the request of the sultan-of-yogyakarta dossier (loss of 1813, counterpart 'pakualaman'). One page opened. Unsettled: (1) the page gives no area or boundary; the outline is two discs (6 and 25 km); (2) the infobox gives no start date, the text says 17 March 1813 and Paku Alam I's reign begins in 1812; (3) the status line 'British rule 1813-1816; dependent state of the Kingdom of the Netherlands 1816-1942' is a suzerainty for british-colonial-empire and dutch-east-indies to record (vassal pairs with this dossier as counterpart); (4) the page does not mention the 1830 Java War; (5) the end: the monarchy joined the Republic in 1945 and the Special Region of Yogyakarta followed in 1950 (the page gives no month for 1945); (6) the Japanese occupation is recorded in the owner's ledger with the occupier as counterpart, the dutch-east-indies convention; (7) capital coordinates approximate. Gazetteer: Adikarta (region), Kulon Progo (regency).
